plan_a_advantages: Consistent, shorter easy runs might be preferable for runners with high injury risk
plan_b_advantages: Dedicated aerobic session for building a stronger base
Slightly longer and more varied easy run durations
reasoning: Both plans prioritize easy running, which is appropriate for a goal of becoming a faster trail runner, but Plan B is superior because it incorporates a dedicated aerobic session. Plan A’s repetitive easy runs without variation risk plateaus and don’t actively build the aerobic base crucial for trail speed. Plan B’s inclusion of a 54-minute aerobic run, even at an easy pace, directly addresses this need, while also providing a slightly longer overall training volume. Furthermore, the slightly longer durations of the easy runs in Plan B (ranging from 25-68 minutes) are more likely to promote consistent aerobic development than the consistent 35-minute runs in Plan A.
